page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.6xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. This CPU features 12 physical cores and 24 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It operates on a KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is provisioned with an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations indicate stable mid-range processing capabilities. The instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1438.39 and a multi-core score of 23015.19. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 1282.13 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 109.43 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and 48.03 GB/sec for large-block writes. In application-specific workloads, the server demonstrated a static web serving throughput of 17.13 GB/sec and processed 22.14 million Redis SET operations per second. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the system processed 1294.61 tokens per second for prompt processing using a small 135M model, though performance scales down to 34.44 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.hfg6.6xlarge offers dedicated CPU resources and a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a stable option for workloads requiring predictable compute performance without the premium of GPU-accelerated or high-memory instances. However, the lack of bundled local storage requires external block storage attachments, which may introduce latency and additional cost. The baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps also limits its utility for highly distributed data-intensive clusters. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and moderate text or image processing tasks.
